model: Standalone Qwen3-8B LoRA24 (q8v5, 6 adapters: f0-f4 + full-fit, plain readout head)
features: LoRA24 Multi-Layer Pooled Representations (Layers [2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24], 32,768d)
compute_config: Kaggle GPU T4 x2, fp16, in-memory dynamic LoRA merge/unmerge
conclusion: SUCCESS: Kaggle public leaderboard verified at 0.606. Delta over EXP45 baseline: +0.157 (+15.7 percentage points). Fast commit < 45s, full inference 16-18 mins. Validated standalone component.
next_recommendation: Proceed to Phase 46B: Blend Qwen3-8B LoRA with 4-View Open Pool LinearSVC (predicted CV 0.675) or add Qwen3-14B LoRA (q14v5) to push past 0.640-0.650 on LB.

research_question: Does adding an unsupervised prompt-recovery centred twin head (twin_weight=0.35) improve attribution accuracy over standalone Qwen3-8B plain head?
hypothesis: Subtracting the prompt cluster mean from multi-layer LoRA features removes common prompt bias and sharpens author-specific identity, improving balanced accuracy without any training or supervision.
dataset_version: Official train.csv (2,699 samples, 150 prompts, 18 LLMs) / Kaggle Test
features: LoRA24 Multi-Layer Pooled Representations (32,768d) + Content-Word TF-IDF Cosine (threshold=0.15, cap=18)
compute_config: Kaggle GPU T4 x2, fp16, in-memory dynamic LoRA merge/unmerge
conclusion: EXP47 implemented and validated. Unsupervised prompt recovery identified 256 multi-passage clusters (2,580 rows) and 119 singletons on train.csv (ARI=0.8670). Singletons reproduce plain logits with 100% exact equality. Local CV improves from 0.5862 to 0.5910 (+0.0048). Awaiting user approval before submission.
next_recommendation: Submit EXP47 to Kaggle to measure empirical gain on LB over EXP46A (0.606).

research_question: Does re-aligning global test column marginals toward training priors via optimal transport improve Balanced Accuracy?
hypothesis: Damping predictions toward balanced priors will lift recall on neglected/subtle classes like kimi-k3 and glm-5.3.
features: LoRA24 (32,768d) + Sinkhorn Scaling
conclusion: Local CV: 0.5910 (+0.0000). Decision: YELLOW. Standalone neural networks are well-calibrated; regularizer retained for heterogeneous ensembles.
next_recommendation: Retain Sinkhorn as regularizer for ensemble methods.

research_question: Does combining deep transformer latent states with surface n-gram stylometry produce orthogonal synergy and break 0.60 BA?
hypothesis: Qwen3-8B captures reasoning semantics while LinearSVC captures tokenizer boundaries; Bayesian logit fusion will slash sibling confusion.
features: LoRA24 (32,768d) + 4-View TF-IDF
conclusion: Local CV: 0.7028 (Nested: 0.6976). Kaggle Public LB: 0.612 (-0.008 vs EXP47 0.620). Over-weighting SVC (85%) caused surface n-gram domain shift on unseen test prompts.
next_recommendation: Cap SVC weight to <= 0.25 (Qwen-dominant) in EXP50.

research_question: Is 4-view surface stylometry from LinearSVC useful as an auxiliary model when Qwen3-8B remains strictly dominant (w_qwen >= 0.75)?
hypothesis: Restricting LinearSVC to an auxiliary tie-breaker role (<= 25% voting mass) will provide regularisation without domain shift.
features: LoRA24 (32,768d) + 4-View Open Pool TF-IDF
conclusion: Local CV: 0.6102 (+0.0193 vs EXP47). Monotonic, fold-consistent gains across all 5 folds while maintaining 97-99% prediction agreement with Qwen.
next_recommendation: Characterize the response surface between 0.20 and 0.50 via EXP50B.

research_question: What is the shape of the Qwen/SVC fusion response surface across w_svc in [0.20, 0.50]?
hypothesis: The response surface may peak between 0.25 and 0.40 before deteriorating, identifying an empirical balance point.
model: EXP47 Qwen3-8B + Open Pool LinearSVC Sweep
features: LoRA24 (32,768d) + 4-View Open Pool TF-IDF
conclusion: Local Balanced Accuracy climbs monotonically to w_svc=0.50 (0.6354 BA). Boundary unresolved at 0.50 due to local logit margin scale mismatch. Conservative w=0.25-0.35 recommended.
next_recommendation: Proceed to deep foundation multi-model scaling with Qwen3-14B in EXP51.

research_question: Does the public LB 0.620 two-stage LoRA recipe on Qwen3-14B provide reproducible attribution signals and complement EXP47?
hypothesis: Scaling foundation model to 14B and truncating to 27 layers captures orthogonal stylistic/semantic features vs 8B.
features: LoRA24 Multi-Layer Pooled Representations (Layers [2, 4, 6, 9, 13, 17, 22, 27], 40,960d)
conclusion: STOP & REPORT COMPLETE (GREEN). Single full-fit checkpoint in Nishant dataset; Anto Pil 5-fold OOF verified at 0.6346 BA. Blended with EXP47 achieves 0.7873 OOF BA (error r=0.0214).
next_recommendation: Verify OOF provenance in EXP51A before building dual-LoRA kernel.

research_question: Are the Qwen3-14B OOF predictions (BA = 0.6346) genuine, leak-free, prompt-disjoint 5-fold predictions?
hypothesis: outputs/oof_q14v5_antopil_lora.csv was generated via strict 5-fold prompt-disjoint CV from distinct fold adapters.
features: LoRA24 40,960d Representations
conclusion: VERDICT: VALID (as q14v5 prompt-disjoint OOF). Cryptographically proved distinct fold heads (heads.pt) and 100% prompt disjointness. Source is Anto Pil q14v5, not Nishant Dahal.
next_recommendation: Proceed to EXP52 dual-LoRA fusion using verified q8v5 and q14v5 adapters.

research_question: Does an ensemble combining Qwen3-8B (q8v5) + Qwen3-14B (q14v5) run within Kaggle GPU limits and reproduce orthogonal gains without surface domain shift?
hypothesis: Replacing shallow LinearSVC with deep 14B sequence model eliminates surface n-gram domain shift while maintaining orthogonal diversity (r=0.0214).
features: Dual LoRA24 Multi-Layer Pooled Representations (32,768d + 40,960d)
compute_config: Kaggle GPU 2x T4 (116 min full run, peak VRAM 10.29 GiB)
conclusion: SUCCESS: Kaggle Public LB verified at 0.632 (+0.012 over EXP47). Sequential execution guarantees zero OOM on dual T4. Current production champion.
next_recommendation: Sweep fusion weights in EXP53.

research_question: Does sweeping Qwen3-14B fusion weight w14 in [0.00, 0.60] reveal an OOF-optimal candidate superior to EXP52 baseline (0.40)?
hypothesis: Exploring 2,000 paired bootstrap resamples will determine whether w14=0.40 is uniquely optimal or if equal weighting (0.50) offers equal power with lower fold variance.
features: Dual LoRA24 Multi-Layer Pooled Representations
conclusion: Verdict: FROZEN. Peak at w14=0.40 (0.7873 BA). Equal weighting w14=0.50 is statistically indistinguishable (-0.0008 BA, p=0.4215). w14=0.60 degrades significantly (p=0.0135). Retain EXP52 at 0.40.
next_recommendation: Maintain EXP52 as frozen production champion.

research_question: Does adding a small contribution from Open Pool 4-view LinearSVC (w_svc <= 0.20) improve the frozen EXP52 ensemble?
hypothesis: Open Pool LinearSVC has low error correlation (r=0.143) with EXP52 and could act as an auxiliary regularizer at small weights (0.05-0.10).
dataset_version: Official train.csv + Open Pool Clean (212,623 passages)
features: EXP52 Deep Logits + Open Pool TF-IDF
conclusion: Verdict: FROZEN. Peak at w_svc=0.05 gives nominal +0.0015 BA (net +4 samples out of 2,699), but 95% bootstrap CI spans zero ([-0.0001, +0.0034]). Not justified given domain shift risk. Retain EXP52.
next_recommendation: Maintain EXP52 as frozen production champion.

research_question: Does an isolated, lightweight stylometry / character-level specialist provide complementary discriminative power to EXP52?
hypothesis: The character-level specialist captures surface orthographic quirks with low error correlation (r=0.115), providing orthogonal regularisation.
features: EXP52 Deep Logits + Char-wb (2-5) and Word Punctuation TF-IDF
conclusion: Verdict: YELLOW. Standalone stylometry achieves only 0.3437 BA. Predefined fusion reaches 0.7899 at w=0.05 (+0.0026); selection-safe nested CV yields 0.7881 +- 0.0098 (delta: +0.0008, CI spans zero). Retain EXP52.
next_recommendation: Maintain EXP52 as frozen production champion.

research_question: Does Qwen3-14B prompt centering residual expose model-specific information that complements EXP52?
hypothesis: Prompt centering against training-only cluster centroids removes prompt-family information and boosts out-of-sample attribution.
features: EXP52 Deep Logits + Prompt Centering Residual
conclusion: Verdict: RED. Standalone residual specialist collapses to 0.1045 BA on held-out prompts due to centroid domain mismatch. Nested CV degrades by -0.0007 BA (0.7866 vs 0.7873). Prompt centering is already optimal in twin head.
next_recommendation: Maintain EXP52 as frozen production champion.

research_question: Does the trained LLM attribution model contain weight-space structure predictive of LLM identity?
hypothesis: Class-specific parameter signatures (norms, singular spectra, cosine alignments) correlate with empirical OOF recall and confusion patterns.
features: LoRA and Readout Weight Tensors
conclusion: Verdict: READ-ONLY DIAGNOSIS. Probe A: ||W_c||_2 vs recall r=0.9528 (p=2.1e-9). Probe B: weight cosine vs pairwise confusion r=0.6176 (p=1.8e-17). Depth-1 Layer-4 discriminator anomaly identified for Gemini 3.7 vs 3.8.
next_recommendation: Validate Probe A causally via norm equalization in EXP57B.

research_question: Does inference-time class-head norm equalization causally correct recall imbalance and improve attribution?
hypothesis: Equalizing class-head L2 norms via W_c / ||W_c||^gamma prevents logit suppression for small-norm classes like GLM and Gemini Flash.
features: Norm-Equalized Classifier Readout Weights
conclusion: Verdict: RED. Refuted causal hypothesis. Standalone gain (+0.0011 at gamma=1.00) is within random permutation noise (65th percentile). Inside EXP52, BA drops from 0.7873 to 0.7847 (-0.0026). Stop weight-space editing.
next_recommendation: Stop weight-space editing. Evaluate early-layer Gemini separation in EXP58.

research_question: Does Qwen3-14B Layer-4 representation contain stable, generalizable information distinguishing Gemini 3.7 Flash from 3.8 Flash?
hypothesis: Peak delta W at Layer 4 (Depth 1) observed in EXP57A represents a generalizable early-layer sibling discriminator on held-out prompts.
dataset_version: 300 Gemini samples across 150 unique prompts in train.csv
model: Qwen3-14B Layer-4 Gemini 3.7 vs 3.8 Linear Probe
features: Layer 4 Pooled Hidden States (5,120d)
conclusion: Verdict: RED. Falsified early-layer hypothesis. Layer 4 BA (0.5367) is substantially worse than full model (0.6067) and within chance null permutation noise (0.4984 +- 0.0278, 90th percentile). Between/within ratio is 0.9946. Peak delta W was in-sample optimizer artifact.
next_recommendation: STOP_GEMINI_EARLY_LAYER_DIRECTION. Retain EXP52 as frozen production champion.

research_question: Why is there a 0.1553 BA gap between EXP52 local OOF (0.7873) and Kaggle Public LB (0.6320)?
hypothesis: Comprehensive 16-stage forensic audit distinguishes between test-set domain shift, prompt density mismatch, and error correlation.
features: Full Logits, Embeddings, Geometry & Error Matrices
conclusion: Verdict: GREEN (Diagnosis Successful). Bitwise inference parity intact. Identified dual drivers: prompt density mismatch (R=18 vs R~2) and inter-backbone error correlation on unseen prompts.
next_recommendation: Execute EXP60 sparse test-regime calibration.

research_question: Does reducing prompt density from R=18 to R=2 explain the 0.1553 BA gap between local OOF (0.7873) and Kaggle LB (0.6320)?
hypothesis: The prompt-recovery / centered-twin mechanism receives unusually strong signal under R=18 validation that collapses under sparse R=2 inference.
features: Plain & Centered Twin Logits across Sparse Subsets
conclusion: Verdict: YELLOW / PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. Plain EXP52 maintains 0.7786 BA under R=2. Twin head attenuates from +0.0044 (dense) to -0.0012 (sparse), diff-in-diff delta delta = +0.0057. Explains 0.0099 BA (6.39% of the 0.1553 gap). 93.61% unexplained gap is driven by general sequence domain shift and positive error correlation.
next_recommendation: Retain EXP52 as frozen production champion at 0.632 LB. Investigate out-of-domain sequence representations and cross-architecture diversification.

research_question: Why is there a 0.1553 BA gap between EXP52 local OOF (0.7873) and Kaggle LB (0.6320)? Is it caused by measurable distribution or representation shift?
hypothesis: The large OOF-to-LB performance gap is caused primarily by measurable distribution/representation shift between the training/local-validation surface and the hidden Kaggle test surface.
cv_strategy: 5-Fold Prompt-Disjoint Stratification, KS Tests, Adversarial Domain Classifier, Matched Local Surface Sweep
features: MiniLM Embeddings, Q8 & Q14 Hidden States, Lexical Statistics
conclusion: Verdict: YELLOW / PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. Covariate shift is negligible (chars d=+0.095, KS p=0.970). Representation distance to training manifold does NOT correlate with attribution error (rho=+0.0071, p=0.712). Matched sparse surface yields 0.7858 BA (sparsity explains <1% of gap). Inter-backbone agreement fragility drives the gap: EXP52 achieves 0.9318 BA when Q8 and Q14 agree vs 0.6871 BA when they disagree (rho=+0.3142, p=6.7e-63). Zero error correlation on train (r=0.0214) collapses on unseen test prompts.
next_recommendation: Retain EXP52 as frozen production champion at 0.632 LB. Investigate non-Qwen architecture diversification (Llama/Gemma/Mistral) and disagreement-aware calibration.

research_question: Does architectural diversity (ModernBERT-base) create genuinely new attribution information that Qwen3-8B + Qwen3-14B do not already contain?
hypothesis: A genuinely different LLM architecture can provide complementary attribution errors that are less correlated with Qwen3-8B/Qwen3-14B, producing a more robust ensemble under unseen-prompt validation.
cv_strategy: 5-Fold Prompt-Disjoint Nested CV (5 outer x 4 inner) + 2000 Bootstrap
features: ModernBERT Frozen Hidden States (768d) + EXP52 Log-Probabilities
conclusion: Verdict: RED. Refuted cross-architecture hypothesis. ModernBERT standalone BA is 0.3093 (LR) / 0.2371 (SVM). Nested CV BA drops from 0.7873 to 0.7858 (delta = -0.0015, 95% CI [-0.0039, +0.0006], P(delta>0)=9.4%). On Q8/Q14 disagreement subset (59.7% of data), ModernBERT achieves only 0.2836 BA (net correction: -662 samples). Low error correlation (r=0.1010) is an artifact of low accuracy rather than useful orthogonality. Stop cross-architecture model stacking.
next_recommendation: Retain EXP52 as frozen production champion at 0.632 LB. Stop un-fine-tuned cross-architecture model stacking.

research_question: Should LLM attribution be modeled as a prompt-conditional relative comparison problem rather than independent classification?
hypothesis: Comparing responses relative to other responses generated for the same prompt removes prompt-specific information, improves classification, and constrained prompt-level set assignment resolves sibling confusions.
cv_strategy: 5-Fold Prompt-Disjoint Nested CV + 5-Seed Sparse Simulation (R in [2..18]) + 2000 Bootstrap
model: Prompt-Conditional Relative Attribution & Hungarian Set Assignment
features: EXP52 Multi-Layer Pooled Logits (Simple Centered, LOO Centered, Pairwise Differences)
conclusion: Verdict: YELLOW. Hungarian 1-to-1 matching reaches 0.9040 BA under dense training construction (R=18, delta = +0.1167, correcting 382/574 EXP52 errors). However, under realistic sparse test simulation (R=2), Hungarian gain completely collapses to +0.0052 BA (0.8021 BA) and LOO relative delta becomes negative (-0.0085 BA). Selection-safe nested fusion yields 0.7995 BA under R=18 (delta = +0.0122, 95% CI [+0.0058, +0.0183]). The massive assignment lift exploits an artificial artifact of dense 18-class prompt construction that is absent in sparse Kaggle test data (R~2).
next_recommendation: Retain EXP52 as frozen production champion at 0.632 LB. Do not deploy Hungarian set assignment to sparse test regimes.

research_question: Can single-sample confidence, margin, and disagreement features route between Q8 and Q14 to outperform fixed 0.60/0.40 fusion?
hypothesis: Although the fixed EXP52 fusion is strong, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B may be reliable on different individual response types; single-sample confidence, margin, entropy, and disagreement may predict which expert is more likely to be correct.
cv_strategy: 5-Fold Prompt-Disjoint Nested CV (5 outer x 4 inner) + 2000 Bootstrap
features: 37 Single-Sample Features (Confidence, Margin, Entropy, Disagreement)
conclusion: Verdict: YELLOW. Nested CV BA is 0.7906 (delta: +0.0033 over EXP52 0.7873). 95% bootstrap CI [-0.0027, +0.0094] spans zero (P(delta>0)=87.0%). On disagreement subset (59.7% of data), corrects 40 errors but degrades 31 correct predictions (net +9 samples). Single-sample invariant to response density.
next_recommendation: Retain EXP52 as frozen production champion at 0.632 LB. Explore diverse architecture sequence fine-tuning.
